fact: 1926年5月3日午夜前一分钟，英国职工大会（TUC）号召全国大罢工，声援被拒于矿井之外的约120万煤矿工人；罢工于5月12日结束，历时9天（各来源对起讫日记法略有差异，但「9天」一致），期间约150万—250万工人停工，包括铁路、码头、印刷、钢铁、煤气、电力与建筑业。

sources.title: BBC, Nine-day strike which brought Britain to a standstill
sources.quote: Beginning at one minute to midnight on 3 May, the strike - called by the Trades Union Congress (TUC) - lasted just nine days, but brought Britain to a standstill. ... in total more than two million workers withdrew their labour in support, including transport workers, dockers and printers.

sources.title: Encyclopedia.com, general strike (May 4–12, 1926)
sources.quote: The strike began at midnight on 3 May, with workers in printing, transport, iron and steel, gas, electricity, and building being called out first. A second group of unions, including engineers and shipbuilders, joined the strike on 11 May; about 2,500,000 workers in total were involved.

sources.title: Ashford Museum, Nine days that stopped Britain
sources.quote: Just before midnight on 3 May 1926, Britain's main trade union body, the Trades Union Congress (TUC), called on workers across the country to stop work. ... The strike ended on 12 May when the TUC believed renewed talks over coal were possible. The miners' lockout, however, continued for months.

fact: 大罢工的直接背景是煤炭业危机与塞缪尔委员会报告：1926年3月10日发布的皇家委员会（主席Herbert Samuel）报告指出，不含补贴时73%的煤炭产量处于亏损；建议重组行业、国有化矿权、按地区定经济工资，并为临时减薪留出空间。矿主据此要求减薪10%—25%并延长工时，矿工以「工资不得少一文，工时不许加一分」拒绝。4月30日煤矿工人被关在矿外，5月1日政府宣布紧急状态。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica 1926 Supplement, Coal Mining（Wikisource）
sources.quote: The report of the Commission, which was unanimous, was issued on March 10 1926. It showed that, excluding the subsidy, 73% of the coal was produced at a loss. ... Although the owners, under pressure, accepted the report in principle, it was rejected by the miners and on Saturday, April 29, the men ceased work.

sources.title: Wikipedia, History of coal miners（1920–45）
sources.quote: The Samuel Commission published a report on 10 March 1926 recommending that in the future, national agreements, the nationalization of royalties, and sweeping reorganization and improvement should be considered for the mining industry. It also recommended a reduction of 13.5% of miners' wages along with the withdrawal of the government subsidy. ... the mine owners declared that, on penalty of a lockout from 1 May, miners would have to accept new terms of employment that included lengthening the work day and reducing wages between 10% and 25%

sources.title: BBC, Nine-day strike which brought Britain to a standstill
sources.quote: A state of emergency was declared by the government on Saturday 1 May, which coincided with a huge rally in central Birmingham

fact: 全国停摆期的物资保障与政府应急运输被如实组织：政府提前招募志愿者与特种警（special constables）维持基本服务，军队卡车运食品并由装甲车护卫，海德公园用作牛奶与面包的分发中心；正常报纸停刊，政府出版官方报纸《British Gazette》，罢工方出版罢工简报，广播（当时问世仅三年）首次显示应急价值。5月8日起业余火车司机开行慢车，志愿者维持伦敦公交与地铁（每名司机配警察防袭）。

sources.title: Look and Learn, The General Strike of 1926
sources.quote: The Army was called in to transport food and blankets. And the public transport was commandeered. ... In London crowds of men assembled in the streets and watched convoys of army trucks loaded with food and guarded by armoured cars, go past. Hyde Park was used as a distribution centre for milk and bread. ... Normal newspapers did not appear and the Government published a daily British Gazette. Broadcasting, three years old, first showed how useful it could be in an emergency. By May 8 amateur train drivers were making slow cross-country journeys. Volunteers manned the London bus and underground services. Each driver had a policeman next to him, to prevent him being attacked by angry strikers.

sources.title: BBC, Nine-day strike which brought Britain to a standstill
sources.quote: As soon as the action was called by the TUC, councils worked to set up emergency committees, opening up registers for volunteer workers to help maintain law and order and keep essential services running. ... Printing workers went on strikes and newspapers were only patchily available

sources.title: Encyclopedia.com, general strike
sources.quote: Stanley Baldwin's government employed special constables and volunteers to run essential services and issued an anti-strike propaganda journal, The British Gazette.

fact: 罢工的直接导火索之一是《每日邮报》印刷工拒绝排印社论，鲍德温政府随即中止谈判；罢工结束后TUC于5月12日收手，期待重启煤炭谈判，但矿工被锁在矿外的局面延续数月，直到1926年11月底多数矿工才在既定减薪与延长工时的条件下复工。1927年《工会法》随后限制了工会权利。

sources.title: Encyclopedia.com, general strike
sources.quote: Baldwin's administration precipitated the strike by breaking off negotiations when the printers at the Daily Mail refused to print a leading article. ... The TUC called off the strike and the Trade Union Act (1927) restricted trade union rights.

sources.title: Wikipedia, History of coal miners
sources.quote: The miners maintained resistance for a few months before being forced by their own economic needs to return to the mines. By the end of November most miners were back at work. ... Those that were employed were forced to accept longer hours, lower wages, and district wage agreements.

fact: 煤炭业危机的数字：矿工工资七年间从每日6先令降到3先令9便士（一说周工资口径从£6降至£3.90），人均年产量从247吨降到199吨；1925年英国回归金本位使英镑偏强、煤炭出口更贵，德国按道威斯计划向法意供「赔款煤」压低了国际煤价。矿工的实际生活水平在1926年前已持续下降。

sources.title: The Independent, What happened the last time Britain downed tools in 1926?
sources.quote: miners' wages had slumped from £6 per day to £3.90 in the post-war era as production fell from 247 tonnes per man per year to 199. ... The country's own use of the fossil fuel had been heavy during the conflict while exports to Europe had ceased, allowing competitors from the US, Poland and Germany to fill the shortfall. Prices for the mineral had also fallen as a result of the Dawes Plan, which required Germany to provide France and Italy – two key markets – with free coal as part of their reparations.

sources.title: Ashford Museum, Nine days that stopped Britain
sources.quote: when Britain returned to the Gold Standard in 1925, it made British exports even more expensive. As profits fell, mine owners pushed for longer hours and lower pay. By 1926, miners were earning far less than before the First World War.

fact: 大罢工期的日常生活：罢工首日即「无火车、无伦敦报纸」；煤炭区的矿工家庭提前进入长期贫困，主妇精打细算使储蓄撑得更久；煤炭城镇的居民甚至烧不起自己挖的煤。1925年7月31日「红色星期五」政府曾拨2300万英镑给煤矿业9个月补贴维持原工资，1926年4月30日补贴用尽后危机爆发。

sources.title: Look and Learn, The General Strike of 1926
sources.quote: In the mining areas, miners' families settled down for a long stretch of poverty. Housewives carefully guarded the family savings so that the money would last longer. ... For another terrible six months the miners held on; their families slowly starving and their clothes in tatters. Winter closed in, and the weather turned cold. But no smoke came from the chimneys of the mining towns. They could not afford the coal they used to mine

sources.title: 环球时报/史海回眸，1926年英国数百万人大罢工（引红色星期五补贴额）
sources.quote: 1925年7月31日,斯坦利·鲍德温的保守党内阁提出由政府出资2300万英镑给煤矿业9个月的特殊津贴,用于维持矿工的原工资水平。 ... 1926年4月30日,政府提供的特殊津贴用尽。当日,煤矿工会就发动了全国煤矿工人大罢工。煤矿工人提出了"工资不得少一文,工时不许加一分"的口号。

fact: 1926年5月1日政府宣布紧急状态，招募特种警（special constables）与志愿者维持秩序与基本服务；罢工期间普通报纸停刊、政府出版《British Gazette》，罢工方出版罢工简报，警方曾搜查共产党地方总部。对穿越者而言：罢工期的集会、出版、驾车都有被盘查的现实风险，参与志愿勤务则需登记并可能获政府证书。

sources.title: BBC, Nine-day strike which brought Britain to a standstill（诺尔·唐宁任特种警、警方搜查共产党总部）
sources.quote: the night before, police had raided the local headquarters of the Communist Party which had been responsible for publishing The Birmingham Worker, one of many daily strike bulletins produced in the absence of newspapers. ... For his two weeks' service Noel, cited as "William Downing", received both a certificate from No 10 Downing Street and also from the Birmingham Watch Committee

sources.title: Encyclopedia.com, general strike
sources.quote: Stanley Baldwin's government employed special constables and volunteers to run essential services and issued an anti-strike propaganda journal, The British Gazette.

fact: 大罢工暴露了英国运输与报业的技术组织方式：铁路与公交靠志愿者与业余司机维持（每车配警察），报纸靠政府刊与罢工简报替代，广播首次在国家应急中发挥作用；政府的应急组织（登记志愿者、分区应急委员会、军队运输）在罢工前已预有准备——这正是罢工九天即败的原因之一。

sources.title: Look and Learn, The General Strike of 1926
sources.quote: Broadcasting, three years old, first showed how useful it could be in an emergency. By May 8 amateur train drivers were making slow cross-country journeys. Volunteers manned the London bus and underground services.

sources.title: Encyclopedia.com, general strike
sources.quote: The strike failed because of government preparations which enabled essential supplies and services to be delivered; many, hostile to the unions, were prepared to assist in breaking the strike; the government won the propaganda battle.

fact: 1926年煤炭业的结构性危机：一战期间英国自身用煤激增、对欧出口中断，美、波、德竞争者填补缺口；战后最优煤层已大量开采、矿主未投资新技术；1925年回归金本位进一步压低出口竞争力。塞缪尔委员会建议小矿合并、销售合作、国家买下矿权、支持低温碳化研究——这些长期改革方向在1926年已明确，但执行者缺位。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica 1926 Supplement, Coal Mining（Wikisource）
sources.quote: the industry should be continued under private enterprise, but state ownership by purchase should be effected of the minerals (royalties) ... Efficient organisation demanded amalgamation of small units of production. Large financial advantages might be gained by the formation of co-operative selling agencies ... If processes of low temperature carbonisation of coal were perfected, great national advantages would ensue because a smokeless fuel would be produced

sources.title: Ashford Museum, Nine days that stopped Britain
sources.quote: Many of the best coal seams had been heavily dug during the First World War, and owners had not invested in new technology. Other countries, like Germany, the United States and Poland, were selling cheaper coal

fact: 煤炭业危机的财政与金融面：1925年7月31日「红色星期五」政府承诺拨2300万英镑给煤矿业作9个月补贴以维持原工资，1926年4月30日补贴用尽即触发罢工与关井；塞缪尔报告指出不含补贴时73%的煤炭产量亏损。政府补贴退出后，亏损矿井的银行敞口与矿主偿付能力成为金融系统的现实风险，部分矿井随后关闭、贷款坏账上升。

sources.title: 环球时报/史海回眸，1926年英国数百万人大罢工（引2300万英镑补贴）
sources.quote: 1925年7月31日,斯坦利·鲍德温的保守党内阁提出由政府出资2300万英镑给煤矿业9个月的特殊津贴,用于维持矿工的原工资水平。 ... 1926年4月30日,政府提供的特殊津贴用尽。当日,煤矿工会就发动了全国煤矿工人大罢工。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica 1926 Supplement, Coal Mining（Wikisource）
sources.quote: It showed that, excluding the subsidy, 73% of the coal was produced at a loss. It condemned the principle of a subsidy. ... This, however, could not prevent the closing of a number of uneconomic collieries, the labour employed at which should be transferred to the "economic" collieries

sources.title: Wikipedia, History of coal miners（矿井关闭与就业下滑）
sources.quote: By the late 1930s, employment in mining had fallen by more than one-third from its pre-strike peak of 1.2 million miners
